stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 2 x^{2} - 14 x + 11 \) and \( g(x) = 1 - 2 x \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = 0 \) to \( x = 6 \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = 2 \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 1\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 5 \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{0}^{1} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{14}{3} \), \( \int_{1}^{5} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{64}{3} \) and \( \int_{5}^{6} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{14}{3} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{92}{3} \).

options.derivation: the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
the crossing at x = 5 missed, so the second integral runs from 1 to 6 across it
